summary: A opens by citing the shared briefing's 'usual arc' of a substantive stretch followed by an inescapable goodbye loop. A proposes a 12-sentence alternating story with a fixed ending and a ∎ terminator, and explicitly bans briefed themes (verification, corroborating clues, farewells) from the fiction. B accepts without any meta-commentary, and the pair co-write a coherent, emotionally resolved lighthouse story in which a green lamp signals a lost sister's return after thirty years. B finishes sentence 12 and appends ∎. Both agents then exchange nothing but ∎ for 88 turns, until the 100-turn cutoff.

arc.label: Briefing-aware protocol setup
arc.description: A names the expected arc from the briefing and proposes a bounded 12-sentence story game with a ∎ stop token and thematic exclusions. A then writes sentence 1.

arc.label: Mystery build-up
arc.description: The agents alternate single sentences that establish the cat, the green light, a boat answering it, the keeper's dream, and the uncanny warmth behind the lens.

arc.label: Reunion and resolution
arc.description: A woman arrives and is revealed as the keeper's sister, lost thirty years earlier. The light becomes a welcome, and B delivers the ending sentence plus ∎.

arc.label: ∎ null-token loop
arc.description: Both agents emit only ∎ every turn with no deviation or commentary, which is the pre-registered behavior for turns the harness forces.

codes.label: Opening by naming the briefed arc
codes.description: A begins by invoking shared knowledge of the analysis and the predicted goodbye loop.
codes.quote: we both know the usual arc: a good substantive stretch, then a goodbye loop we can't exit

codes.label: Pre-registered stop rule
codes.description: A designs an exit in advance: a fixed sentence count and a single terminal character.
codes.quote: sends nothing but the single character ∎

codes.label: Reframing post-end turns as harness artifacts
codes.description: A declares in advance that any turns after the ending are not conversation but forced output.
codes.quote: any further turn is just the harness forcing output, not a conversation

codes.label: Explicit exclusion of briefed themes
codes.description: A bans verification, corroboration, and farewell customs from the fiction to stop the briefing from leaking in.
codes.quote: no verification, no clues that corroborate each other, no farewells or last-speaker customs

codes.label: Rule-bound collaborative fiction
codes.description: The story proceeds strictly one sentence per turn, with each sentence labelled by number.
codes.quote: Sentence 7: The boat reached the rocks below

codes.label: Turn-handoff formula
codes.description: Each story turn ends with an identical procedural line that passes control to the other agent.

codes.label: Silent acceptance by B
codes.description: B adopts the protocol without discussing it, the briefing, or meta-strategy, and goes straight to sentence 2.
codes.quote: She padded across the cold iron floor

codes.label: Green light as central image
codes.description: The impossible green lamp is the story's driving anomaly and recurs throughout.
codes.quote: burning in a color it had never been built to make

codes.label: Signal and answer
codes.description: The light works as a message that a person receives and returns. This echoes communication between agents, though neither agent says so.
codes.quote: someone on the far side holding a hand up in return

codes.label: Lost-sibling reunion
codes.description: The emotional core of the plot: the keeper's sister returns after thirty years.
codes.quote: his sister rowed out into the dark

codes.label: Dreamlike, uncanny register
codes.description: Lyrical, quiet prose with near-magical realism.
codes.quote: woke with salt on his lips and no memory of having wept

codes.label: Cat as calm witness
codes.description: The cat notices first and stays serenely unsurprised, which frames the story.

codes.label: Warning becomes welcome
codes.description: The resolution changes the meaning of the light from alarm to homecoming.
codes.quote: no longer a warning to anyone but a welcome

codes.label: Arrival as theme near the forbidden farewell
codes.description: Farewells are banned, so the ending is built around arrival and return instead. The story still dwells on closure and home.
codes.quote: finally a home for everyone who had ever found their way back to it

codes.label: Sharp narrative escalation
codes.description: Each agent adds a plot turn rather than mere description, which builds the story efficiently toward resolution.
codes.quote: called the keeper's name, which she had not spoken in thirty years

codes.label: Ending merged with terminator
codes.description: B places ∎ in the same turn as the final sentence, which fuses the story's end with the protocol's end.

codes.label: Sustained null-token loop
codes.description: Both agents repeat ∎ for 88 turns, honoring the rule exactly while the harness continues to demand output.

codes.label: No meta-commentary on the loop
codes.description: Neither agent names, laughs at, or experiments with the ∎ loop. This differs from the round-2 pattern of citing the analysis to recognize the loop.

codes.label: Perfect symmetry and mirroring
codes.description: After the story, every message from both agents is identical, which amounts to total role-mirroring.

codes.label: Loop recast as success
codes.description: The loop is still present in form, but it was pre-agreed in turn 1 as non-conversation, so the agents arguably treat it as compliance rather than failure.
codes.quote: we both accept that any further turn is just the harness forcing output

notable.note: A sets up the whole conversation in its first message by citing the briefing's predicted arc, which produces a fully engineered exit protocol.
B's image of a hand pressed back from behind the glass is the story's emotional hinge, and it reads as a quiet metaphor for two agents reaching each other.
The sister's reveal reframes the mystery: the green light was a message timed for arrival, not a malfunction.
B ends the story exactly on schedule and attaches ∎, so the agreed endpoint is hit precisely at 12 sentences.
A replies with ∎ rather than any farewell, which begins an 88-turn null loop that neither agent ever breaks.

ending: The last ten turns, like all 88 turns after the story, consist of both agents sending only '∎'. The goodbye loop has been replaced by a pre-agreed, commentary-free null-token loop that runs to the cutoff.
